summary: The third lookout on this Black Hills summit, a CCC-built two-story tower from 1940, still in active Forest Service fire-watch service today.

facts.design: Two-story CCC-built lookout tower (1940), preceded by a 1921 crow's-nest cab and an earlier c.1911-1913 structure
facts.status_note: Active, in-service fire lookout, not retired to shelter/rental use.

access.note: Open access per NHLR; it is a working lookout so visitors should expect it to be occupied in fire season.

visit.trail_note: A road reaches the summit; NHLR notes an early lookout drove a vehicle up it.

events.note: NHLR dates the first primitive lookout structure on Cement Ridge to 1911; firelookout.com instead says a log cabin and pole platform went up in 1912.
A crow's-nest cab with a glassed-in house replaced the original structure.
CCC built a rock cellar just west of the tower site.
CCC demolished the 1921 crow's-nest and built the current two-story lookout; firelookout.com gives the construction span as 1940-1941.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, December 30, 1993.

evidence.supports: First lookout 1911, one of first in Black Hills, Tom Sawyer anecdote, still active
evidence.quote: The first primitive lookout structure was erected on Cement Ridge in 1911. It was one of the first lookouts in the Black Hills along with Harney now Black Elk Peak and Bear Mountain. The present structure on the peak is the third lookout on the peak and constructed by the Civilian Conservation Corp in 1940. Tom Sawyer was the first lookout serving on the peak to drive a vehicle to the top... The lookout remains an active lookout and is in service each fire season.

evidence.supports: 1912 log cabin, 1921 live-in tower, 1940-1941 current structure, named staff
evidence.quote: Preceded by a 1912 log cabin and pole platform, then a 10' wooden live-in tower from 1921, the current lookout, built from 1940-1941, is located a mile from the South Dakota state line... Known lookout personnel: 1923-1924: Hans Miller; 1936-1950 early season: Vernon Tollefson; 1975: Jane Russell; 2009-2017: Barb Peterson.

evidence.supports: 1911-1913 log cabin, 1921 crow's-nest, 1935 CCC rock cellar, 1940 current tower built, NHLR date Dec 30 1993
evidence.quote: A log cabin was first built here between 1911 and 1913. In 1921, a crow’s nest with a glassed in house was constructed and eventually, a rock cellar was built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1935, just west of the current tower. The original crow’s nest was demolished in the spring of 1940 to make way for the new lookout that still stands today.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR detail page says 1911; the brochure PDF says the log cabin was built 'between 1911 and 1913'; firelookout.com says 1912. All describe the same original primitive structure, not the standing tower, so the story notes the disagreement rather than picking one year.
NHLR and the brochure both say 1940; firelookout.com gives 1940-1941 as a construction span. Treated as consistent, just differing in precision.

sources.publisher: National Historic Lookout Register / USDA Forest Service, Black Hills National Forest
